Mise en garde officielle de Brid Algérie: Official warning from Brid Algérie against digital scams
L’Entreprise Poste Algérie (Brid Algérie: The public industrial and commercial establishment (EPIC) Algérie Poste (Brid Algérie) has published a vigilance notice addressed to its customers to raise awareness about the risks associated with phishing attempts. The institution reminds users that it never requests confidential information by phone or electronic messages, such as secret codes or passwords, including OTPs (One-Time Passwords) used to validate online transactions.
Dans le même temps, Brid Algérie appelle: At the same time, Brid Algérie is calling on citizens to exercise caution in the face of suspicious calls or SMS, emphasizing the importance of never sharing personal data (bank card numbers, login credentials, etc.) and reporting any fraudulent behavior without delay via the company's official channels. These measures are part of a national cybersecurity awareness campaign, in collaboration with the Postal and Electronic Communications Regulatory Authority (ARPCE) and Algerian mobile operators.
Analyse et enjeux pour l'Algérie : une l: Analysis and stakes for Algeria: an intensified fight against cybercrime
La multiplication des tentatives d’arnaq: The proliferation of digital scam attempts in Algeria, notably via fraudulent calls or messages imitating official services, reflects a 40% increase in online fraud reports between 2024 and 2025, according to data from the ANPT (National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data). These practices, often orchestrated by international criminal networks, particularly target users who are unfamiliar with digital tools. For Algeria, where the internet penetration rate reached 125% in 2025 (representing over 60 million mobile subscribers and 32 million fixed users), securing online transactions has become a strategic challenge for economic and social development.
Les conséquences de ces fraudes sont mul: The consequences of these frauds are manifold: financial losses for individuals and businesses, damage to the reputation of public institutions, and a brake on the adoption of digital services. The Algerian government, via the Digital Plan 2030, has placed cybersecurity at the heart of its priorities, with a budget of 12 billion dinars allocated to modernizing Algérie Télécom's infrastructure and training citizens. Similar campaigns have already reduced online fraud cases by 25% in certain wilayas, such as Algiers or Oran, thanks to awareness workshops organized by the APCs (Municipal People's Assemblies).
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien : entre: Context of the Algerian ICT sector: between expansion and vulnerabilities
L’Algérie affiche une croissance soutenu: Algeria is showing sustained growth in its telecommunications sector, with a mobile penetration rate exceeding 125% in 2025, according to the latest statistics from ARPCE. The country now has 32 million fixed and mobile internet subscribers, of which 28 million use smartphones, a figure in constant progression thanks to the expansion of 4G and 5G networks driven by operators such as Mobilis SA, Djezzy, and Ooredoo Algérie. The government has accelerated the deployment of fiber optics, with 15,000 km of cables installed in 2025, covering 80% of the country's municipalities.
Cependant, cette digitalisation rapide s: However, this rapid digitalization comes with major security challenges. Algérie Télécom, the historic operator, invested 8 billion dinars in 2025 to strengthen its cybersecurity infrastructure, notably through the deployment of a national computer emergency response team (CERT) and the training of 5,000 agents dedicated to the fight against cybercrime. ANPT, for its part, launched a digital trust label for businesses in 2024 to encourage the adoption of best practices in data protection. Despite these advances, experts emphasize the need for enhanced coordination between public and private stakeholders to stem the threat of online fraud.
The General Manager of Brid Algérie, Mr. Mohamed El Hachemi, reaffirmed the company's commitment to protecting its customers' data: "The safety of citizens is our absolute priority. We urge everyone to remain vigilant and to report any attempted fraud via our official platforms, notably our mobile application or our website." Meanwhile, the President of ARPCE, Mr. Abdellatif Khedraoui, recalled that "the fight against cybercrime is a collective mission that requires the mobilization of all stakeholders, including citizens."
Pour renforcer la résilience du secteur,: To strengthen the sector's resilience, Brid Algérie plans to launch a dedicated online fraud-reporting platform by the end of 2026. This initiative, developed in partnership with ARPCE and mobile operators, will allow users to report scam attempts in real time via an online form or mobile application. At the same time, the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications announced the deployment of 1,200 contact points across the wilayas to provide direct assistance to citizens.
Sur le plan réglementaire, une révision: On the regulatory front, a review of the legal framework is underway to stiffen penalties for perpetrators of online fraud, with fines of up to 50 million dinars and mandatory prison sentences.
